deck.title: RDS & Aurora
deck.analogy: Multi-AZ is the spare tire (for when things go wrong); Read Replicas are extra supermarket checkout lanes (more customers served every day).

cards.front: What is RDS and which engines does it support?

back.answer: RDS is AWS-managed relational database: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, or SQL Server.
back.explanation: AWS handles patching, backups and hardware replacement.

cards.front: Does RDS give OS-level access? What if a question needs it or a custom engine?

back.answer: No OS access. Use database on EC2, or RDS Custom (Oracle/SQL Server).
back.explanation: You can't SSH in, install OS-level extensions or tweak engine binaries on plain RDS.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: replication type?

back.answer: Multi-AZ is synchronous; Read Replicas are asynchronous (slight lag).
back.explanation: Multi-AZ standby is always exactly current.
back.mnemonic: Multi-AZ = spare tire; Read Replicas = extra checkout lanes.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: where do the copies live?

back.answer: Multi-AZ: standby in another AZ. Read Replicas: same AZ, cross-AZ, or cross-Region.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: how many copies?

back.answer: Multi-AZ: 1 standby. Read Replicas: up to 15.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: can you read from the copy?

back.answer: Multi-AZ standby: no reads at all. Read Replicas: yes, via read-only endpoints.
back.explanation: Serving reads is the whole point of replicas.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: how does failover work?

back.answer: Multi-AZ: automatic, 60–120s via DNS flip. Read Replica: no automatic failover; manual promotion only.
back.explanation: The DNS flip keeps the same endpoint with a new machine behind it.

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas: what does each solve?

back.answer: Multi-AZ solves AZ failure and hardware death; Read Replicas solve read-heavy workloads and reporting.
back.explanation: Production uses both; they aren't competitors.

cards.front: Trap: can the RDS Multi-AZ standby serve read traffic?

back.answer: No. The standby is invisible until failover.
back.explanation: The spare tire stays in the trunk.

cards.front: Trap: does an RDS Read Replica provide automatic failover?

back.explanation: A cross-region replica is a budget DR plan, but not automatic.

cards.front: RDS automated backups: what do they enable and what is the max retention?

back.explanation: They are deleted when the instance is deleted.

cards.front: How long do RDS manual snapshots last, and when do you use them?

back.answer: Kept until you delete them; use for retention beyond 35 days (e.g. 5 or 7 years, compliance).
back.explanation: 35 days is the wall automated backups can't cross.

cards.front: When can you enable encryption on an RDS database?

back.answer: Only at creation; it can't be flipped on in place.
back.explanation: You also can't encrypt the original snapshot directly; you encrypt the copy.

cards.front: How do you encrypt an existing unencrypted RDS database?

back.answer: Snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, restore from the encrypted copy, repoint the app.
back.explanation: Encryption is creation-time only, so the copy carries it.
back.code: unencrypted DB → snapshot → COPY the snapshot (enable encryption) → restore from encrypted copy → repoint the app

cards.front: What is RDS Proxy and why is it needed with Lambda?

back.answer: A connection pool in front of RDS; thousands of clients share a small warm set of connections.
back.explanation: Lambda scales to thousands of executions and would exhaust database connections.

cards.front: Besides pooling, how does RDS Proxy help during failover?

back.answer: It shrinks failover time by holding client connections and re-routing them.
back.explanation: Clients don't each re-resolve DNS.

cards.front: RDS keeps running out of disk with unpredictable growth. What feature helps?

back.explanation: RDS grows storage automatically when it runs low.

cards.front: What is Aurora's key architectural trick?

back.answer: It separates compute from storage: all nodes share one storage layer of 6 copies across 3 AZs.
back.explanation: Storage is self-healing and auto-grows to 128 TB; compute nodes are disposable.

cards.front: Aurora failover time vs RDS Multi-AZ?

back.answer: Aurora under 30 seconds; RDS Multi-AZ 60–120 seconds.
back.explanation: A reader that already sees all data is promoted.

cards.front: Aurora replica count and lag vs RDS replicas?

back.answer: Up to 15 replicas with ~millisecond lag; RDS replicas are async with seconds of lag.

cards.front: Aurora engine compatibility and max storage?

back.answer: Compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL; storage auto-grows to 128 TB.

cards.front: What are Aurora's two endpoints?

back.answer: Writer endpoint (current writer, survives failover) and reader endpoint (load-balances across replicas).
back.explanation: Never hardcode instance addresses.

cards.front: Which Aurora feature suits spiky, unpredictable or idle workloads?

back.explanation: Capacity scales itself and you pay for what you use, e.g. dev/test used a few hours a day.

cards.front: Which Aurora feature gives cross-region DR with RPO ~1s and RTO <1 minute?

back.explanation: Also gives local low-latency reads on other continents. A plain cross-region read replica is slower: the budget distractor.

cards.front: What does Aurora Cloning do?

back.answer: Copy-on-write instant copy of a production database, with no storage duplication.
back.explanation: A full-size staging/test copy in minutes.

cards.front: What does Aurora Backtrack do, and which engine?

back.answer: Rewinds the database in place (Aurora MySQL) without restoring from backup.
back.explanation: Undo an accidental delete or bad migration fast; no new instance.

cards.front: Define RPO and RTO.

back.answer: RPO: how much data you may lose. RTO: how long until you're back.
back.explanation: Aurora Global Database is ~1s RPO, <1min RTO.

cards.front: Database must survive an AZ failure with no manual intervention. Which RDS feature?

back.explanation: Survive failure + automatic = 60–120s DNS flip.

choices.why: Automatic failover to a standby in another AZ.

cards.front: Reporting/analytics queries (diverse, complex) slow the production RDS database. Best fix?

back.explanation: If the same queries repeat, ElastiCache wins instead.

cards.front: Lambda functions are exhausting RDS database connections. Fix?

back.explanation: Lambda + RDS = Proxy.

cards.front: How do you encrypt an existing unencrypted RDS database?

back.explanation: Encryption is creation-time only.

choices.why: Only the copy can be encrypted.

choices.text: Add a Read Replica with encryption

cards.front: Global app needs cross-region DR with less than 1 minute recovery. Which service?

back.explanation: RPO ~1s, RTO <1min.

cards.front: Dev database sits idle nights and weekends; minimize cost. Which option?

back.explanation: Spiky/idle/unpredictable = serverless.

cards.front: Need a full copy of the production Aurora database for testing, quickly and cheaply?

back.explanation: Copy-on-write: instant, near-free until it diverges.

cards.front: Developer ran a bad DELETE; restore Aurora to 5 minutes ago as fast as possible?

back.explanation: Rewind in place; no restore, no new instance.

choices.text: PITR restore to a new cluster

cards.front: Compliance requires RDS database backups kept for 7 years. What do you use?

back.explanation: Automated backups cap at 35 days.

cards.front: Application needs OS-level access / a custom database engine. What do you choose?

back.answer: Database on EC2 (or RDS Custom for Oracle/SQL Server).
back.explanation: Plain RDS gives no OS access.

choices.why: Full control of OS and engine.

back.answer: Read Replica (async, up to 15, manual promotion)
